title: Natives Land Act, South Africa, 1913
summary: The Natives Land Act (Act No. 27 of 1913) came into effect on 19 June 1913. It barred Africans from buying or hiring land outside designated areas, confining them to about 7 percent of the country, and curtailed tenant farming and sharecropping on white-owned farms. It began the legal pattern of land dispossession later built on by apartheid.

uncertainty.note: Sources state the Act was passed and came into effect on 19 June 1913. Full enforcement was delayed and its effects unfolded over later years.

beats.caption: The Natives Land Act (No. 27) came into effect on 19 June 1913.
Africans were barred from buying or hiring land in about 93 percent of South Africa, leaving them about 7 percent.
The 1936 Native Trust and Land Act raised the share for Africans to 13.5 percent, still a small fraction of the country.
